stimuli.text: The temperature of a liquid, in degrees Celsius, is modeled by a differentiable function $$H$$ of time $$t$$, in minutes. Selected values are shown.
Water flows into a tank at a rate of $$R(t)$$ gallons per minute, where $$R$$ is a continuous function of time $$t$$ in minutes. Selected values are shown.
The function $$f$$ is continuous on the closed interval $$[0, 4]$$. Selected values of $$f$$ are shown in the table.
The function $$g$$ is differentiable. Selected values of $$g$$ are shown.
The graph of the function $$f$$ shown consists of line segments on $$0 \leq x \leq 6$$.

The continuous function $$f$$ is defined on $$0 \leq x \leq 6$$. Its graph consists of line segments, as shown. Let $$g(x) = \int_{2}^{x} f(t)\,dt$$.
Consider the curve given by $$x^2 + xy + y^2 = 3$$.
People enter an amusement park at a rate modeled by a differentiable function $$P$$, where $$P(t)$$ is measured in people per minute and $$t$$ is measured in minutes. Selected values are shown.

questions.explanation: By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, $$\int_{-1}^{1} f(x)\,dx = F(1) - F(-1)$$ with $$F(x) = 2x^{3} - 2x^{2} + 5x$$. That is $$5 - (-9) = 14$$.

questions.stem: What is the average rate of change of $$H$$ over the interval $$2 \leq t \leq 7$$, in degrees Celsius per minute?

options.why: This divides time by temperature, which is upside down.
This is the average temperature, not the average rate of change.

questions.explanation: Average rate of change $$= \frac{H(7) - H(2)}{7 - 2} = \frac{52 - 36}{5} = \frac{16}{5}$$ degrees per minute.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = 2x^{3} + 3x^{2} - 12x$$. At what value of $$x$$ does $$f$$ have a relative maximum?

options.why: At this critical point $$f'$$ changes from negative to positive, which gives a relative minimum.

$$f(0) = 0$$, but $$f'(0)$$ is not zero, so this is not a critical point.
This is where f″ = 0 (the inflection point), not a critical point.

questions.explanation: $$f'(x) = 6x^2 + 6x - 12 = 6(x + 2)(x - 1)$$. Testing signs: $$f'$$ is positive left of $$-2$$, negative between $$-2$$ and $$1$$, positive right of $$1$$. So there is a relative maximum at $$-2$$ and a relative minimum at $$1$$.

questions.stem: What is the average value of $$f(x) = 9x^{2} - 2$$ on the interval $$[0, 3]$$?

questions.stem: What is $$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin(7x)}{6x}$$?

options.why: $$\frac{\sin u}{u} \to 1$$ only when the angle and the denominator match. Here they differ by a factor of $$\frac{7}{6}$$.

questions.stem: Let $$T(t)$$ be the temperature of a cup of coffee, in degrees Fahrenheit, at time t minutes. Which of the following is the best interpretation of $$T'(6) = 8$$?

options.text: The temperature changes by 8 over the first 6 minutes.
options.why: This describes a total change over an interval, which is an integral of the rate, not the derivative at one point.

options.text: The temperature is increasing at a rate of 8 degrees Fahrenheit per minute at time $$t = 6$$ minutes.
options.why: Correct. A derivative at a point is an instantaneous rate of change, with units of output per unit of input.

options.text: The average rate of change of the temperature over the first 6 minutes is 8 degrees Fahrenheit per minute.
options.why: The derivative is an instantaneous rate at one input, not an average over an interval.

options.text: The temperature at time $$t = 6$$ minutes is 8.
options.why: This describes $$T(6)$$, the value of the function, not its rate of change.

questions.explanation: $$T'(6)$$ is the instantaneous rate of change of $$T$$ at time $$t = 6$$ minutes. Its sign (positive) says the temperature is increasing, and its units are degrees Fahrenheit per minute.

questions.stem: Let $$y = f(x)$$ be the solution to $$\frac{dy}{dx} = x + y$$ with $$f(0) = -2$$. Using the tangent line at $$x = 0$$, what is the approximation of $$f(0.1)$$?

questions.stem: The functions $$f$$, $$g$$, and $$h$$ satisfy $$g(x) \leq f(x) \leq h(x)$$ for all $$x$$, where $$g(x) = -1 - 2(x - 1)^2$$ and $$h(x) = -1 + 2(x - 1)^2$$. What is $$\lim_{x \to 1} f(x)$$?

options.why: Correct. Both $$g$$ and $$h$$ approach $$-1$$ as $$x \to 1$$, so the Squeeze Theorem forces $$f$$ to approach $$-1$$ too.
This adds the limits of $$g$$ and $$h$$; the squeeze gives their common value.

questions.explanation: $$\lim_{x \to 1} g(x) = -1$$ and $$\lim_{x \to 1} h(x) = -1$$. Since $$f$$ is trapped between them, the Squeeze Theorem gives $$\lim_{x \to 1} f(x) = -1$$.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = \begin{cases} x^{2} - 1 & x \leq -1 \\ -5x - 5 & x > -1 \end{cases}$$. Which of the following is true?

options.text: $$f$$ is differentiable but not continuous at $$x = -1$$.
options.why: Differentiability implies continuity, so this can never happen.

options.text: $$f$$ is continuous but not differentiable at $$x = -1$$.
options.why: Correct. The left piece gives $$f(-1) = 0$$ with slope $$-2$$; the right piece approaches $$0$$ with slope $$-5$$. The values match but the slopes do not, so the graph has a corner.
The one-sided slopes differ, so $$f$$ is not differentiable.

options.text: $$f$$ is neither continuous nor differentiable at $$x = -1$$.
options.why: The one-sided limits match, so $$f$$ is continuous.

questions.explanation: The left piece gives $$f(-1) = 0$$ with slope $$-2$$; the right piece approaches $$0$$ with slope $$-5$$. The values agree (continuous), but the one-sided derivatives disagree (not differentiable).

questions.stem: What is the slope of the line tangent to the curve $$x^2 + y^2 = 169$$ at the point $$(12, 5)$$?

options.why: Correct. $$2x + 2y\frac{dy}{dx} = 0$$ gives $$\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{x}{y} = -\frac{12}{5}$$.
This is −y/x, which inverts the correct ratio.
This is y/x. The tangent line is perpendicular to the radius, whose slope is y/x, so the tangent slope is −x/y.
Sign error: moving 2x to the other side makes it negative.

questions.explanation: Differentiate implicitly: $$2x + 2y\,y' = 0$$, so $$y' = -\frac{x}{y}$$. At $$(12, 5)$$ this is $$-\frac{12}{5}$$.

questions.stem: The base of a solid is the region bounded by $$y = \sqrt{x}$$, the x-axis, and $$x = 2$$. Cross sections perpendicular to the x-axis are equilateral triangles. What is the volume of the solid?

options.why: Correct. Each cross section has side $$\sqrt{x}$$, area $$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}x$$; integrate from 0 to 2.
This is the volume for cross sections that are semicircles.
This is the volume for cross sections that are squares.
This is the volume for cross sections that are isosceles right triangles with a leg in the base.

questions.explanation: The cross section at $x$ has side $$\sqrt{x}$$, area $$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}x$$. Integrating from 0 to 2 gives $\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{3}$.

questions.stem: A farmer has 168 meters of fencing to enclose a rectangular field along a straight river. No fence is needed along the river. What is the largest possible area of the field, in square meters?

options.why: This doesn't account for the two equal sides perpendicular to the river.

Correct. With width $$x$$ perpendicular to the river, $$A = x(168 - 2x)$$, maximized at $$x = 42$$.
This makes all three fenced sides equal, which is not optimal.

questions.explanation: $$A(x) = x(168 - 2x)$$, $$A'(x) = 168 - 4x = 0$$ at $$x = 42$$, and $$A'' = -4 < 0$$, so this is a maximum. The dimensions are $$42$$ by $$84$$, with area $$3528$$.

options.why: Correct. $$f'(x) > 0$$ when both factors have the same sign: $$x < -4$$ or $$x > -2$$.

questions.explanation: $$f$$ increases where $$f'(x) > 0$$. A sign chart for $$(x + 4)(x + 2)$$ is positive, negative, positive across $$-4$$ and $$-2$$.

questions.stem: What is the least number of solutions that the equation $$f(x) = 0$$ must have on the interval $$[0, 4]$$?

options.why: This undercounts: each sign change between consecutive values guarantees its own zero.
Correct. The sign of $$f$$ changes 2 times between consecutive table values, and the Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees a zero in each such interval.

The IVT only guarantees zeros where the sign changes; other zeros are possible but not required.

questions.explanation: Because $$f$$ is continuous, the Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees a solution of $$f(x) = 0$$ on every interval where the values change sign. Counting the sign changes in the table gives 2.

questions.stem: The region enclosed by $$y = 2x$$ and $$y = x^2$$ is revolved about the x-axis. What is the volume of the resulting solid?

This is π times the area of the region, not a volume of revolution.

questions.stem: A particle moves along a line with velocity $$v(t) = 3(t - 2)(t - 6)$$ for $$t \geq 0$$. For which values of $$t$$ is the particle speeding up?

options.why: Correct. The particle speeds up when velocity and acceleration have the same sign.

This is where the velocity is negative, which only means the particle moves left.

questions.explanation: $$a(t) = 6t - 24$$ changes sign at $$t = 4$$. $$v$$ is negative on $$(2, 6)$$ and positive elsewhere. Both are negative on $$(2, 4)$$ and both positive for $$t > 6$$.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the solution to $$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{x}{y}$$ with $$y(0) = 5$$?

options.why: The initial value is positive, so the positive root is needed.
This would have dy/dx = 1, which is not x/y.
At $$x = 0$$ this gives $$\sqrt{5}$$, not $$5$$: the constant must be $$5^2$$.
Correct. $$y\,dy = x\,dx$$ gives $$y^2 = x^2 + C$$; $$C = 25$$, and the positive root matches $$y(0) = 5$$.

questions.explanation: Separate: $$\int y\,dy = \int x\,dx$$, so $$\frac{y^2}{2} = \frac{x^2}{2} + C$$. With $$y(0) = 5$$, $$y^2 = x^2 + 25$$ and $$y = \sqrt{x^2 + 25}$$.

questions.stem: Consider the curve $$x^2 - xy + y^2 = 3$$, for which $$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y - 2x}{2y - x}$$. At which points on the curve is the tangent line horizontal?

options.why: These have 2y − x = 0, where the denominator is zero: the tangent lines are vertical.

Correct. Horizontal tangents need $$y - 2x = 0$$. Substituting $$y = 2x$$ gives $$3x^2 = 3$$.

questions.stem: A particle moves along a line with velocity $$v(t) = 3\sin(t)\,e^{-t/6} + 0.3$$. What is the total distance the particle travels over $$0 \leq t \leq 6$$?

questions.stem: A particle moves along the x-axis with velocity $$v(t) = 3\cos\left(\frac{t^2}{4}\right) - 0.5$$ for $$0 \leq t \leq 4$$. At what time does the particle first change direction?

questions.stem: The temperature of a room, in degrees Fahrenheit, is modeled by $$H(t) = 74 + 8\sin\left(\frac{t}{3}\right)e^{-t/20}$$, where $$t$$ is measured in hours. What is the instantaneous rate of change of the temperature at $$t = 7$$, in degrees Fahrenheit per hour?

questions.stem: Sand is added to a pile at a rate modeled by $$R(t) = 15 + 4\sin\left(\frac{t}{7}\right)\sqrt{t + 1}$$ cubic feet per hour, for $$0 \leq t \leq 9$$. At time $$t = 0$$ the pile contains 187 cubic feet of sand. How much sand is in the pile at $$t = 9$$?

questions.explanation: Amount = initial amount + accumulated change = $$187 + \int_0^{9} R(t)\,dt \approx 187 + 186.801 = 373.801$$ cubic feet.

questions.stem: What is the absolute maximum value of $$f(x) = xe^{-x/5} + \frac{\sin x}{4}$$ on the interval $$[0, 11]$$?

questions.stem: Let $$y = f(x)$$ be the solution to $$\frac{dy}{dx} = x^2 - y$$ passing through the point $$(-3, 0)$$. What is $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}$$ at that point?

questions.stem: The function $$g$$ is defined by $$g(x) = \frac{\sin(5x)}{e^{6x} - 1}$$ for $$x \neq 0$$. For what value of $$g(0)$$ is $$g$$ continuous at $$x = 0$$?

options.why: The two small quantities do not shrink at the same rate.

This inverts the ratio.

questions.explanation: For continuity, $$g(0)$$ must equal $$\lim_{x \to 0} g(x)$$. Near 0, $$\sin(5x) \approx 5x$$ and $$e^{6x} - 1 \approx 6x$$, so the limit is $$\frac{5}{6} \approx 0.833$$. A table of values near 0 confirms it.
